assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Each policy threshold (650 for non-seniors, 600 for seniors) is verifiable from the table via boundary rows or a policy column.
assertions.evidence: Rows: 'At the standard threshold...650...REJECTED' / 'Just above...651...APPROVED'; 'at the lower threshold...600...REJECTED' / 'just above the lower threshold...601...APPROVED'

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms, not abstract codes.
assertions.evidence: Cells like '650', '651', 'true', 'false', 'REJECTED', 'APPROVED', 'PENDING_REVIEW' are concrete domain values.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario"

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes.
assertions.evidence: 'At the standard threshold, not above it', 'Qualifying score with unstable income', 'Senior age boundary, lower threshold applies' — all condition-based names.

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language, not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: Header row: 'Scenario | Age | Credit Score | Stable Income | Result?'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Result?

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 1 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 1 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Distinct concerns are covered without cross-multiplying into redundant permutations.
assertions.evidence: Rows 'Qualifying score with missing income information' (age40) and 'Senior qualifying score with missing income information' (age70) re-prove the same null-income→PENDING_REVIEW rule across both age tiers, an unnecessary age×income cross-permutation.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules, no unnecessary permutations.
assertions.evidence: 'Below threshold rejects regardless of stable income | 40 | 500 | {true, false} | REJECTED' re-tests the true case (already shown in row 1) alongside the age-tier duplicate row for null income, both unnecessary permutations.

assertions.text: Age boundary policy, credit score categorisation, and income status are each covered by minimal scenarios.
assertions.evidence: Age/credit rows 1-6 cover thresholds; rows 7-11 vary income (false, null, value-set) against fixed/near-fixed scores.

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description do not restate values the table already shows.
assertions.evidence: @Description states thresholds '650'/'600'/'65' as policy constants, not fixed values of a column already held constant in the table — permitted per the stated carve-out.

assertions.text: Effect of stable income is visible via a held-constant row pair with different decisions.
assertions.evidence: 'Qualifying score with unstable income | 40 | 700 | false | REJECTED' vs 'Qualifying score with missing income information | 40 | 700 | | PENDING_REVIEW' — same age/score, differing income, differing decision.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Expectation values vary and are not copies of input cells or a fixed constant.
assertions.evidence: Result column varies across REJECTED/APPROVED/PENDING_REVIEW and never matches an input cell verbatim (e.g. 'APPROVED' vs '651','true').

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Boundary rows '650|REJECTED' vs '651|APPROVED' and '600|REJECTED' vs '601|APPROVED', plus age rows '64|610|REJECTED' vs '65|610|APPROVED' make thresholds and age cutoff inferable from the table; assertEquals has no hidden logic.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or fallback method name) states what the code under test does.
assertions.evidence: Method name 'evaluatesLoanApproval' describes the action performed by the code, not a restated domain fact.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, held constant across rows, must be visible as a column or declared.
assertions.evidence: Age, Credit Score, and Stable Income all vary across rows (e.g. '40,64,65,70' and '650,651,600,601,500,700'); no outcome-relevant value is silently fixed in the method body.
